title: Hypothermia
summary: Too cold: shivering, confused, or soaked in the cold. Stop heat loss and rewarm safely.
sources: Wilderness Medical Society Clinical Practice Guidelines for Out-of-Hospital Evaluation and Treatment of Accidental Hypothermia
U.S. Army FM 21-76 / ATP 3-50.21 Survival (cold-weather injuries)
firstLine: Get the person out of wind, water, and wet ground now. Handle them gently. Send someone to call for help if you can.

nodes.help: Cold slows breathing a lot. Watch and listen carefully for up to 1 full minute before deciding.

options.label: Shivering hard, but thinking and talking clearly
Confused, clumsy, slurring, very drowsy, or shivering has stopped

nodes.title: Mild hypothermia - rewarm
steps: Get them into shelter, out of the wind.
Replace wet clothing with dry layers. If you can't, wrap a plastic or foil layer over the wet clothes to stop evaporation.
Insulate from the ground with pads, packs, or branches. The ground steals more heat than the air.
Give warm, sugary drinks and high-calorie food if they can swallow safely. Shivering burns fuel.
Light activity is OK once they are dry and fed, if they are steady on their feet.
Share body heat in a sleeping bag if needed.
doNot: Do not keep pushing on in wet clothes hoping to warm up by moving.

options.label: Yes, warming up and shivering less
No, or getting confused or drowsy

nodes.title: Moderate or severe hypothermia
steps: Handle them very gently. Rough movement can trigger a fatal heart rhythm.
Keep them lying flat. Do not let them walk or stand.
Cut off wet clothing rather than pulling it off, if you can do it without exposing them for long.
Make a hypothermia wrap: insulation underneath, a sleeping bag or blankets around, and a plastic or foil layer outside, covering the head and leaving the face open.
Place warm water bottles or heat packs wrapped in cloth on the chest, armpits, and back. Not directly on skin.
Only give sugary drinks if they are alert enough to swallow safely.
doNot: Do not rub or massage arms and legs.
Do not put them in a hot bath or shower.
Do not give food or drink if they are drowsy or confused.

nodes.title: Recovering from mild hypothermia
steps: Keep them dry, fed, and insulated. Keep them in shelter until fully rewarmed.
Fix what caused it (wet clothes, no shelter, not enough food) before moving on.
Watch the rest of the group. If one person is hypothermic, others may be close.

nodes.title: Evacuate - severe hypothermia
steps: This person needs a hospital. Evacuate lying flat, wrapped, and handled gently.
Check breathing every few minutes, watching up to a full minute each time.
If breathing stops, start CPR. Someone severely hypothermic can survive long CPR.
If they become alert and start shivering, that is a good sign. Keep them wrapped.

nodes.title: Not breathing - start CPR
steps: Start CPR now and use an AED if available.
Hypothermic patients can survive prolonged CPR. Do not give up early if it is safe to continue.
Keep them insulated from the ground and wrapped as much as CPR allows.
